questions.question: What is a business requirement?

choices.A: A restriction on the design or implementation choices open to the developer
choices.B: A top-level requirement for a product built from several interacting subsystems
choices.C: A policy, guideline, standard, or regulation that constrains the business
choices.D: A nonfunctional requirement describing a service characteristic such as speed
choices.E: A statement of a property or characteristic the system is required to respect
choices.F: A high-level objective explaining why the organization wants the product

questions.explanation: A business requirement states the objective the organization is trying to reach by having the product built.

questions.question: What is a business rule?

choices.A: A policy, guideline, standard, or regulation that constrains the business
choices.B: A statement of the behavior the system performs under a specific condition
choices.C: A description of a connection between the system and an outside device or program
choices.D: A goal or task a defined class of users must be able to accomplish with the system
choices.E: A set of logically related capabilities that together deliver value to a user
choices.F: A high-level objective explaining why the organization wants the product

questions.explanation: A business rule comes from policy, regulation, or how the organization operates. It often leads to software requirements but is not one itself.

questions.question: What is a constraint?

choices.A: A restriction on the design or implementation choices open to the developer
choices.B: A high-level objective explaining why the organization wants the product
choices.C: A policy, guideline, standard, or regulation that constrains the business
choices.D: A statement of the behavior the system performs under a specific condition
choices.E: A statement of a property or characteristic the system is required to respect
choices.F: A set of logically related capabilities that together deliver value to a user

questions.explanation: A constraint narrows the set of design or implementation choices the developer is allowed to make.

questions.question: What is an external interface requirement?

choices.A: A statement of the behavior the system performs under a specific condition
choices.B: A policy, guideline, standard, or regulation that constrains the business
choices.C: A restriction on the design or implementation choices open to the developer
choices.D: A description of a connection between the system and an outside device or program
choices.E: A top-level requirement for a product built from several interacting subsystems
choices.F: A high-level objective explaining why the organization wants the product

questions.explanation: External interface requirements cover connections to users, other software systems, and hardware devices.

questions.question: What is a feature?

choices.A: A policy, guideline, standard, or regulation that constrains the business
choices.B: A statement of the behavior the system performs under a specific condition
choices.C: A high-level objective explaining why the organization wants the product
choices.D: A set of logically related capabilities that together deliver value to a user
choices.E: A description of a connection between the system and an outside device or program
choices.F: A goal or task a defined class of users must be able to accomplish with the system

questions.explanation: A feature groups related capabilities and is normally described by several functional requirements.

questions.question: What is a functional requirement?

choices.A: A set of logically related capabilities that together deliver value to a user
choices.B: A goal or task a defined class of users must be able to accomplish with the system
choices.C: A policy, guideline, standard, or regulation that constrains the business
choices.D: A statement of the behavior the system performs under a specific condition
choices.E: A restriction on the design or implementation choices open to the developer
choices.F: A description of a connection between the system and an outside device or program

questions.explanation: A functional requirement states what the system does, under what condition, in terms a developer can build against.

questions.question: What is a nonfunctional requirement?

choices.A: A statement of a property or characteristic the system is required to respect
choices.B: A nonfunctional requirement describing a service characteristic such as speed
choices.C: A restriction on the design or implementation choices open to the developer
choices.D: A goal or task a defined class of users must be able to accomplish with the system
choices.E: A top-level requirement for a product built from several interacting subsystems
choices.F: A description of a connection between the system and an outside device or program

questions.explanation: Nonfunctional requirements describe properties and restrictions rather than behavior the system carries out.

questions.question: What is a quality attribute?

choices.A: A description of a connection between the system and an outside device or program
choices.B: A nonfunctional requirement describing a service characteristic such as speed
choices.C: A statement of the behavior the system performs under a specific condition
choices.D: A statement of a property or characteristic the system is required to respect
choices.E: A set of logically related capabilities that together deliver value to a user
choices.F: A restriction on the design or implementation choices open to the developer

questions.explanation: A quality attribute is one kind of nonfunctional requirement, covering service characteristics like performance or security.

questions.question: What is a system requirement?

choices.A: A goal or task a defined class of users must be able to accomplish with the system
choices.B: A restriction on the design or implementation choices open to the developer
choices.C: A high-level objective explaining why the organization wants the product
choices.D: A statement of the behavior the system performs under a specific condition
choices.E: A statement of a property or characteristic the system is required to respect
choices.F: A top-level requirement for a product built from several interacting subsystems

questions.explanation: System requirements apply to a whole product made of interacting parts, which may include hardware as well as software.

questions.question: What is a user requirement?

choices.A: A statement of the behavior the system performs under a specific condition
choices.B: A policy, guideline, standard, or regulation that constrains the business
choices.C: A nonfunctional requirement describing a service characteristic such as speed
choices.D: A set of logically related capabilities that together deliver value to a user
choices.E: A statement of a property or characteristic the system is required to respect
choices.F: A goal or task a defined class of users must be able to accomplish with the system

questions.explanation: User requirements describe what a user needs to accomplish, not the detailed software behavior that supports it.

questions.question: Discord wants to raise weekly engagement by making it easier for communities to stay active. What type of requirement is this?

choices.C: User requirement
choices.D: Nonfunctional requirement
choices.E: Business requirement
choices.F: Quality attribute

questions.explanation: It states why the organization wants the work done and what value it expects in return.

questions.question: Instagram accounts must belong to someone at least thirteen years old, per company policy and law. What is that policy?

choices.C: Nonfunctional requirement
choices.D: Functional requirement
choices.E: System requirement
choices.F: Business rule

questions.explanation: The age policy exists outside the software. Instagram then needs functional requirements that enforce it.

questions.question: The Netflix app must run on smart TVs that shipped in 2018 with limited memory. What is the MOST specific classification?

choices.C: System requirement
choices.D: Functional requirement
choices.E: Nonfunctional requirement
choices.F: Feature

questions.explanation: Existing hardware removes implementation options from the developer, which is what a constraint does.

questions.question: Instagram lets outside applications publish posts through its Graph API. What does that connection represent?

choices.C: System requirement
choices.D: External interface requirement
choices.E: Quality attribute
choices.F: Nonfunctional requirement

questions.explanation: The Graph API is a connection between Instagram and separate software systems.

questions.question: Discord's Server Moderation covers banning, kicking, muting, and role permissions. What is Server Moderation best classified as?

choices.C: Functional requirement
choices.D: Nonfunctional requirement
choices.E: System requirement
choices.F: External interface requirement

questions.explanation: It names a group of related capabilities that deliver value together, which is a feature.

questions.question: When a user submits a prompt, ChatGPT shall stream the reply back token by token. What type of requirement is this?

choices.C: External interface requirement
choices.D: Business requirement
choices.E: Nonfunctional requirement
choices.F: Feature

questions.explanation: It names a specific behavior triggered by a specific condition.

questions.question: Google Search should return a results page within half a second at peak traffic. What is the MOST specific classification?

choices.C: Quality attribute
choices.D: Feature
choices.E: External interface requirement
choices.F: User requirement

questions.explanation: Response time under load is a service characteristic, so quality attribute is more specific than nonfunctional requirement.

questions.question: A first-time Netflix viewer must be able to find and start a show without being shown how. Which quality attribute is this?

choices.C: Maintainability
choices.D: Availability
choices.E: Usability
choices.F: Reliability

questions.explanation: Usability covers how easily a new user can learn the product and finish a task correctly.

questions.question: A Google Maps user needs to find out whether a nearby pharmacy is open right now. What type of requirement is this?

choices.C: Business requirement
choices.D: System requirement
choices.E: User requirement
choices.F: Nonfunctional requirement

questions.explanation: It describes a task a user class needs to accomplish, without saying how the software provides it.

questions.question: Instagram shall reject a sign-up whose entered birth date puts the person under thirteen. What is this statement?

choices.C: Functional requirement
choices.D: Feature
choices.E: Quality attribute
choices.F: Business requirement

questions.explanation: The age policy is the business rule. This statement is the software behavior that enforces it.

questions.question: Discord runs as desktop, mobile, and web clients plus backend services, databases, and voice infrastructure. A top-level requirement covering that whole arrangement is called what?

choices.C: System requirement
choices.D: Feature
choices.E: Quality attribute
choices.F: Business rule

questions.explanation: The requirement applies to a product assembled from several interacting subsystems.

questions.question: Discord's permission model says only a role holding Manage Messages may delete another member's post. What is that model?

choices.C: Business requirement
choices.D: Nonfunctional requirement
choices.E: Constraint
choices.F: Functional requirement

questions.explanation: The permission policy is the rule. Functional and security requirements are then written to enforce it.

questions.question: Which of these are functional requirements for Discord? Select all that apply.

choices.A: Discord shall serve one hundred thousand concurrent users without slowdown
choices.B: Discord shall remove a message when a moderator with permission deletes it
choices.C: Discord wants to raise the number of servers a typical user stays active in
choices.D: Discord shall deliver a text message to every member who can view the channel
choices.E: Discord shall notify a member when someone mentions them inside a channel
choices.F: Discord shall run on smart TV browsers built before the 2019 model year

questions.explanation: The first three name behavior the software performs. The others are a quality attribute, a business requirement, and a constraint.

questions.question: Which of these are nonfunctional requirements for Netflix? Select all that apply.

choices.A: Netflix must keep a profile's viewing history readable only to that account
choices.B: Netflix must stay available during the evening peak in every served region
choices.C: Netflix must begin playback within two seconds of a viewer pressing play
choices.D: Netflix shall let a subscriber add a title to the My List collection
choices.E: Netflix must keep playing when a client briefly loses its network connection
choices.F: Netflix shall show the ten most relevant results for a search query

questions.explanation: Performance, security, availability, and robustness describe characteristics. The other two describe behavior.

questions.question: Which of these are stated at the level of a user requirement? Select all that apply.

choices.A: A shopper needs to find the seller behind a product tagged in a photo
choices.B: A viewer needs to keep a story private to the people they already follow
choices.C: The API shall return 403 when the caller lacks the manage_posts permission
choices.D: The client shall page the feed in batches of twenty using a cursor token
choices.E: The server shall write a StoryView row for each unique viewer of a story
choices.F: A creator needs to know which of their posts drew the most saves this week

questions.explanation: The first three name goals a user class has. The others are system behavior stated for a developer.

questions.question: Which of these would be external interfaces for Spotify? Select all that apply.

choices.A: The recommendation engine inside the Spotify backend
choices.B: A car head unit connecting over Android Auto or CarPlay
choices.C: A Bluetooth speaker the phone hands the audio stream to
choices.D: The policy that free accounts must hear ads each hour
choices.E: A smart TV app casting playback from the phone client
choices.F: A third-party app pulling playlists through the Web API

questions.explanation: External interfaces are devices, outside software, and users beyond the system boundary. An internal module is not external, and a policy is a business rule.

questions.question: A feature and a functional requirement mean the same thing.
questions.explanation: A feature bundles related capabilities and is usually described by several functional requirements.

questions.question: A business rule can exist even if no software ever enforces it.
questions.explanation: Business rules come from policy, regulation, or standards. Software requirements may be written to enforce them.

questions.question: Every quality attribute is a nonfunctional requirement.
questions.explanation: A quality attribute is defined as one type of nonfunctional requirement.

questions.question: Every nonfunctional requirement is a quality attribute.
questions.explanation: Constraints and external interface requirements are also nonfunctional but are not quality attributes.

questions.question: "A moderator needs to remove a disruptive member" and "Discord shall show moderators a Ban Member action" sit at the same level.
questions.explanation: The first is a user goal. The second is a specific product behavior proposed to support it.

questions.question: A constraint reduces the number of implementation choices open to the developer.
questions.explanation: That is the defining idea behind a constraint.

questions.question: A subscriber tells Netflix: "I don't care how it works, I just want it to pick up where I stopped, on whatever screen I grab next." Which statement is the USER requirement?

choices.A: Netflix shall raise average weekly viewing hours per subscriber by ten percent
choices.B: Sync playback position over the device presence channel already open per client
choices.C: A viewer needs to resume a title on any device from the point where they stopped
choices.D: Write the last playback position to the profile record after every heartbeat
choices.E: Add a GET /titles/:id/progress endpoint that returns the saved timestamp value
choices.F: Store playback progress keyed by profile and title in the existing datastore

questions.explanation: A user requirement names what the user needs to accomplish and leaves the implementation open.

questions.question: For that same request, which statement is the best FUNCTIONAL requirement?

choices.A: Subscribers want a smoother experience when they switch between their devices
choices.B: Netflix shall resume playback at the last position saved for that profile
choices.C: Cassandra fits this well because the writes are cheap and the reads are keyed
choices.D: Cross-device continuity is the most requested improvement from subscribers
choices.E: A viewer needs to keep watching without hunting for where they left off
choices.F: Playback progress ought to live somewhere durable rather than on the client

questions.explanation: It states observable system behavior without naming a business goal, a user goal, or a specific technology.

questions.question: Which sequence runs from the highest-level reason for a product down to detailed software behavior?

choices.A: Business requirement, then functional requirement, then user requirement
choices.B: Functional requirement, then user requirement, then business requirement
choices.C: User requirement, then functional requirement, then business requirement
choices.D: User requirement, then business requirement, then functional requirement
choices.E: Business requirement, then user requirement, then functional requirement
choices.F: Business rule, then business requirement, then external interface requirement

questions.explanation: Why the business wants it, then what users must accomplish, then what the system does.

questions.question: One business requirement can give rise to several user requirements.
questions.explanation: A single business objective usually breaks down into multiple user goals and many functional requirements.

questions.question: Nonfunctional requirements are optional and can be dropped when the schedule slips.
questions.explanation: They are requirements. Dropping one changes what the delivered product is required to be.
